import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (primary key)
# Aggregations:
# - fare: mean (float)
# - ride_id: mean (float)
# - driver_count: max (integer) (driver_count is from source0, same city has same driver_count, max to keep that)
agg_df = joined.groupby("city").agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean",
    "driver_count": "max"
}).reset_index()

# Ensure column order and types as target schema
agg_df = agg_df[["city", "fare", "ride_id", "driver_count"]]

# Cast types to match target schema
agg_df["city"] = agg_df["city"].astype(str)
agg_df["fare"] = agg_df["fare"].astype(float)
agg_df["ride_id"] = agg_df["ride_id"].astype(float)
agg_df["driver_count"] = agg_df["driver_count"].astype(int)

# Write output
agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
